title: The sp Hybridization of Tin Single Atoms for Dendrite-Free Sodium Metal Batteries
text:
The universal synthesis of fourth main group single atoms (Sn, Ge, Pb) anchored on graphene with sp hybridization was reported for dendrite-free sodium metal batteries. In situ real-time observation showed kinetically uniform planar deposition of Na on Sn SAs/G, substantially suppressing dendrite growth. The symmetrical Sn SAs/G-Na battery exhibited 99.8% Coulombic efficiency for 200 cycles, long-term cyclability of 600 h at 4 mA cm-2, and an ultralow overpotential of 40 mV at 8 mA cm-2. Full batteries Na3V2(PO4)3 || Sn SAs/G-Na showed 67 mAh g-1 at 20 C and 91% capacity retention after 500 cycles.

Graphene oxide was used as the support to anchor atomically dispersed Sn single atoms. Sn content was 2.93 wt% and the specific surface area was 543 m2 g-1. XANES and XPS indicated a +4 valence state of Sn. FT-EXAFS showed that the Sn center atom was coordinated with four ether oxygens and one hydroxyl oxygen. In situ TEM showed uniform Na growth on Sn SAs/G, while Na dendrites appeared on pure graphene and Na nanoparticles formed on Ni SAs/G.

DFT calculations revealed that Sn SAs/G had a Na adsorption energy of -1.49 eV, stronger than Ni, Zn, Fe, and Co single atoms on graphene. The 5s2 5p2 electron configuration of Sn led to sp2-like hybridization and favored planar Na3 cluster growth along the graphene plane. Ge SAs/G and Pb SAs/G also inhibited Na dendrite growth, showing the generality of fourth main group elements.
